reveal.auditorReaction: You estimated a score of 50, and Sherpas clocks you at 60 (-10 gap). You have tremendous income and liquid assets, but an 18% credit card and an open $1.1M life insurance shortfall are dragging down an otherwise strong foundation.

discoveries.title: THE 18% PARADOX
discoveries.source: Key Metrics — Debt Management & Cashflow Statement
discoveries.explanation: You hold $150,800 in accessible liquid cash, but carry an $18,000 credit card balance at 18% APR. Your monthly payment of $300 sends $270 directly to interest charges, keeping you on a 12-year treadmill until 2039 unless restructured.
discoveries.whyItMatters: Your cash above the full 9-month emergency reserve ($84,577) is over $60,000. Holding onto high-interest credit card debt when you have free cash is effectively paying 18% guaranteed penalty fees.
discoveries.auditorRemark: Your savings are doing a heroic job sitting there. Your credit card, meanwhile, is working overtime against you. Let us stop paying the bank an 18% subscription fee for keeping cash in a checking account.

discoveries.title: THE $1,100,000 PROTECTION VOID
discoveries.source: Key Metrics — Life Insurance Coverage Analysis
discoveries.explanation: Timothy has $140,000 in coverage (shortfall of $610,000) and Melanie has $110,000 in coverage (shortfall of $490,000). With Liam (6) and Josh (3) relying on both high incomes, existing coverage covers less than 1 year of earnings.
discoveries.whyItMatters: If either earner experiences an unexpected life event, household cash flow would face an immediate deficit before Liam and Josh even reach middle school.
discoveries.auditorRemark: You have protected your peace of mind with cash, but left your children unprotected against the one catastrophe cash cannot absorb alone.

discoveries.title: THE EMPTY 529 ACCOUNTS
discoveries.explanation: Liam enters college in August 2038 and Josh in August 2041. Total projected inflation-adjusted funding gap is $113,508.60, requiring $4,609/year in dedicated savings starting today.
discoveries.whyItMatters: Every year of delay means college funding will collide with your peak retirement accumulation window.
discoveries.auditorRemark: College seems far away until it is next August. Setting up the automatic contribution today is vastly cheaper than liquidating brokerage assets in 2038.
